purpose: Review future research thresholds with a complete model-refit simulation; do not change already registered gates or reclassify the first observed batch.
timing: Written after the initial historical batch was inspected, before synthetic calibration/power results.
baseline_mean: -0.2 * latest forecast wind; no added feature signal under the null
overlapping_cohorts: The same NFL game receives the same synthetic outcome in revision and style cohorts; NFL and CFB noise draws are independent.
effect_feature: revision residualized on wind using the first five predictor seasons, then standardized on those same initial seasons
inference: Use exactly the 23 paired comparisons and season-balanced two-sided t statistics from the parent protocol; selection also requires positive mean improvement.
max_t_calibration: Per noise regime, use independent null calibration replicates for the 95th percentile of the maximum positive t statistic. Evaluate on separate seeds and replicates; thresholds are simulation-specific future-study diagnostics.
fit: Refit coefficients on earlier seasons for EVERY synthetic outcome vector, then score the next season. Cache only fixed design matrices and matrix factorizations, algebraically equivalent to independent ridge fits. No coefficient or loss is reused across simulated outcomes.
data: Historical predictor rows through 2025 only; no final-score columns needed. Fixed predictor distributions are conditional simulation inputs, not a fresh confirmation sample.
limits: All-null any-selection is family-wise false discovery probability. Under nonzero effects, any-selection is not FDR or a true-discovery count: several candidates may capture the planted effect. BH requires appropriate dependence assumptions. This experiment evaluates a fixed 23-comparison prospective family, not the full historical 314-specification search. Scoring effects are not betting returns.
decision: Compare false-positive calibration and power. Prepare a recommendation separating discovery from independent confirmation. Do not automatically select the highest-power method or amend any live rule. Additional model specifications or empirical fair-price alternatives still require trial accounting.
